sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Dedicated Offshore Software Engineering and Maintenance Hub

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state company registers or separate commercial courts)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Franco-Belgian codified tradition under the Civil Code and the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; the SCSp was introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016 and incorporates Anglo-American partnership-law flexibility).
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) - People's Republic of China BIT (signed 2003, entered into force 2007)
US-Luxembourg Income Tax Treaty (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by Protocols of 2004 and 2009)
Luxembourg-Germany DTA of 23 August 1958 (as amended by the Protocol of 2007)
Luxembourg-France DTA of 1 April 1958 (as amended in 2006)
Hague Convention Abolishing the Requirement of Legalisation for Foreign Public Documents of 5 October 1961 (in force for Luxembourg since 30 June 1979)
EU-Canada Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) and EU framework trade agreements applicable to Luxembourg

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et contre le financement du terrorisme), as last amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 and the Law of 10 July 2020; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2019 on RBE implementing modalities; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (Articles 101-108 as amended by the Law of 23 July 2016) governing the SCSp.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (in practice: the RBE is no longer publicly searchable following the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 in joined cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 and the Luxembourg Constitutional Court decision of 9 June 2023; access is limited to competent authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), and obliged entities performing CDD; nominee/back-to-back arrangements must be disclosed and do not exempt registration).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or extract of the foreign register for the corporate general partner or ultimate parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Delaware Division of Corporations, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (1961 Convention) issued by the competent Ministry or originating registry; if the origin state is not a Convention party, consular legalization at the Luxembourg Embassy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized and apostilled power of attorney for the Luxembourg domiciliation agent and external counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if the origin state is a signatory of the 1961 Convention; otherwise chain notarization followed by consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of residential address of all ultimate beneficial owners, general partner(s), and authorized managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent administrative authority of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization depending on the origin state; copies must be notarized within 30 days prior to submission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of non-action from the foreign registry for the corporate general partner or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization if the origin state has not acceded to the 1961 Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds evidence covering the initial capital contribution to the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution of the contributor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized bank letter; apostille required only if the bank reference is embedded in a notarized affidavit submitted to Luxembourg authorities

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn translation into French, German, or English of foreign-language constitutional documents (LPA drafts, passports, corporate instruments)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg Court of Appeal or an accredited translator in the origin state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of the translator's signature; the translation itself is then annexed to the notarial deed without a separate apostille

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD under CSSF Regulation 12-02 and the AML Law of 12 November 2004: (i) identify and verify every UBO holding 25% or more of the partnership interests or exercising control through any other means; (ii) screen UBOs, general partner, managers, and authorized signatories against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP), OFAC SDN list (required for USD and Wise-B2B clearances), and the Luxembourg national sanctions and RBE criminal-record database; (iii) determine PEP status pursuant to the FATF 12-month cooling-off rule; enhanced due diligence and senior-management approval are mandatory for foreign and domestic PEPs, high-risk third countries, or any adverse media hit; (iv) verify source of funds and source of wealth by independent and reliable documentation for the initial contribution; (v) maintain a written AML risk file, update the residual risk assessment at least annually, and report any suspicion to the CRF without delay under Article 5 of the AML Law.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - official online platform at www.lbr.lu, operated jointly with the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of Luxembourg.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed name must be composed of Latin-alphabet characters (a-z, 0-9, limited punctuation) and must be pronounceable in one of the administrative languages (French, German, Luxembourgish) or in English. Non-Latin scripts (Cyrillic, Arabic, CJK characters) are not registrable; a sworn linguistic certificate is required where the name is transliterated from a non-Latin origin. The name must include the statutory suffix 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or the abbreviation 'SCSp'. The name must not mislead as to the legal form, must not create confusion with an existing RCS-registered name or a prior trademark, and must not contain a domain-style suffix unless expressly approved.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial LBR name reservation is valid for 60 calendar days from the date of granted reservation. A single renewal of 60 days may be requested through the LBR online dashboard before the initial expiry; no further extension is granted. If the reservation lapses, the name may be claimed by a third party and the applicant must submit a fresh reservation accompanied by the applicable fee. Upon rejection, the applicant may: (i) within 15 days of the refusal file a written administrative reconsideration request with the LBR, annexing evidence of prior trademark rights, written consents of the holders of sensitive tokens, and a revised alternative name; (ii) within three months of the final refusal bring an annulment action before the Tribunal administratif (administrative chamber) pursuant to the amended Law of 7 November 1996, with a legal submission on the grounds of excess of power or infringement of the Law of 10 August 1915; and (iii) in parallel immediately submit a new reservation for a revised name to protect the projected incorporation timetable.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. The SCSp is not subject to a physical-presence requirement under the Law of 10 August 1915; however, a verifiable street address in Luxembourg must be declared in the RCS filing and a P.O. box is expressly rejected. A commercial virtual-office arrangement is acceptable only where the domiciliation agent holds an authorization under Article 5 of the Luxembourg Law of 31 May 1999 (agrément) and where the books, records, and UBO documentation of the SCSp remain physically or electronically accessible in Luxembourg upon request of the RCS, the Administration des Contributions Directes, or the CRF.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: LOW for the first 12 months (estimated 5-8%) and MODERATE over 36 months (estimated 18-25%). The CRF and the Tax Administration may conduct unannounced on-site inspections where RBE data discrepancies, suspicious source-of-funds indicators, or economic-substance red flags arise. For a passive, tax-transparent offshore software development hub with no Luxembourg employees, the probability of an inspection in the first 12 months is estimated at 8%, increasing to approximately 25% where the entity engages in high-volume intra-group invoicing or where a counterparty triggers a CRF reporting event.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS name search and name reservation fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per the LBR fee schedule (EUR 70)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified (sworn) translation of foreign constitutional documents, passports, and UBO evidence
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator registered with the Luxembourg Court of Appeal

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation (acte authentique) for the SCSp
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notaries tariff (tarif des notaires) and prevailing market scale (EUR 2,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting and negotiation of the Limited Partnership Agreement (LPA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 3,000, fixed fee scope)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR / RCS incorporation registration filing fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013, Articles 901-1 to 901-16 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); implementing Grand-Ducal regulations on the Luxembourg Business Registers and electronic filing.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessible via the eJustice.lu electronic filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Duly signed limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) and registration declaration (déclaration de constitution) filed electronically with the RCS.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum legal capital is prescribed for an SCSp. Limited partners are not subject to a mandatory paid-in amount, and no escrow account is required by law. Contributions are contractually fixed in the partnership agreement; opening a bank account may impose separate commercial funding conditions.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the partnership interests subscribed respectively by the general partner and initial limited partners are hereby accepted, and the subscription register and account of contributions are approved; (2) that the registered office of the SCSp is established at [address], Luxembourg, and minutes/notifications are filed with the RCS; (3) that [Name] is appointed manager/gérant with full power to represent and bind the SCSp, including opening bank accounts and executing service contracts; (4) that the manager is authorized and directed to complete all statutory filings and licenses necessary for the offshore software development center, and to engage service providers as required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Reserve corporate name and draft SCSp partnership agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – online name/RCS consultation; Luxembourg notary or qualified legal counsel (optional)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary name availability check through the LBR search database or instruct counsel. Draft the SCSp limited partnership agreement containing the legal form, name, registered office in Luxembourg, purpose (software programming, maintenance and consultancy services under ISIC 6202), identity and contributions of partners, manager/gérant, signatory rules, and profit-sharing provisions. Execute the agreement as a private deed, or as a notarial deed where required by the bank or counterparties.
required_dossiers: Draft SCSp partnership agreement (statut / contrat de société)
Identity and proof of address of general and limited partners
Identity of prospective manager/gérant
Power of attorney if a representative is signing
AML/KYC source-of-funds information
Name availability verification record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses the name or requests clarifications, submit alternative names or amend the partnership agreement and resubmit. A formal objection may be cured by filing a revised deed with a short explanatory cover note to the LBR.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Luxembourg bank account and arrange initial contributions
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank in Luxembourg; no government window involved
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed partnership agreement, KYC package and business context to the chosen Luxembourg bank. The bank opens an account in the name of the SCSp and records the subscription contributions according to the agreement. Obtain a bank confirmation or account-opening certificate for internal records if required by counterparties.
required_dossiers: Executed SCSp partnership agreement
Certified identities of all partners and the manager
LBR/RCS extracts if already registered
Bank KYC forms and AML declaration
Confirmation of contribution or bank account certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank requests additional economic substance information, provide a short business plan, anticipated clients, and payroll projections. If the bank declines the file despite adequate documentation, approach another licensed Luxembourg bank or escalate through the relationship manager.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File registration with Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS through eJustice.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to eJustice.lu or the RCS digital filing portal and complete the registration workflow for a société en commandite spéciale. Attach the signed partnership agreement, identify the general partner, limited partners, manager/gérant, and registered office in Luxembourg. Pay the applicable filing fee online. The RCS verifies formal completeness and issues the RCS registration number.
required_dossiers: Signed SCSp partnership agreement (private act or notarial deed)
RCS registration declaration
Identification details of all partners and manager/gérant
Signed consent of the appointed manager
Registered office consent from the landlord or address provider
Proof of payment of filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or rejection, respond within the notified deadline through the portal, supply corrected wording or additional signed consents, and resubmit. Any defect in the partnership agreement may be rectified by a private amending instrument deposited as part of the cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain RESA publication and official RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After successful RCS registration, the RCS arranges publication of the required legal notice in the RESA. Download and archive the RESA publication and the official RCS extract or certificate of registration, which together evidence the SCSp's existence, registry number, manager, and registered office.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
RCS extract / certificate of incorporation
RESA publication record
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains typographical or legal inaccuracies, request a rectification from LBR by providing a comparative schedule. If the extract is delayed, request an expedited extract through the LBR portal or contact the registry directly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for tax, VAT and social security formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Administration des contributions directes (ACD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the business registration via the RCS data transfer to obtain the Luxembourg business identification number. Register for VAT with the AEDT only if the SCSp performs taxable supplies not covered by reverse-charge or outside scope; register as an employer with the CCSS when personnel are hired. Provide the tax file with the partnership agreement so that the tax-transparent treatment is properly reflected at the level of partners.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
SCSp partnership agreement and partner list
Bank account confirmation
Employer registration data and individual work contracts
Power of attorney for the responsible tax representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT challenges the VAT treatment, submit a written place-of-supply analysis showing cross-border B2B services. If the CCSS notifies missing filings, complete the overdue employer declaration and pay any interest promptly to avoid further enforcement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure office premises and confirm unregulated business status
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal commune (registered office location); Ministry of the Economy – Direction de l'administration des classes moyennes (authorisation confirmation only if specifically requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that software engineering, programming, and offshore development center services are not regulated activities requiring an establishment authorization in Luxembourg. Ensure the registered office is physically or administratively located at the declared address, with a lease or occupancy title, appropriate fire safety arrangements, and an emergency plan suitable for an office-based ICT service company.
required_dossiers: Lease agreement or ownership title for premises
Business plan / description of services
Proof of registered office address
Fire safety and building occupancy certificates
Data protection and IT security policies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the commune requests an occupancy permit or imposes local fire safety upgrades, obtain the necessary municipal approval and arrange a follow-up inspection. If the Ministry of the Economy asks for confirmation of the unregulated nature of the activity, supply the relevant ISIC/NACE reference and legal basis excluding the activity from the regulated professions regime.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable – software programming and offshore development centre services are not classified as industrial establishments under Luxembourg law. For ordinary office occupation, municipal building and fire authorities are the only relevant public bodies.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No specific industrial operating licence is required for an offshore software development centre; a standard office lease, business registration, and fire safety sign-off are sufficient.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category Exempt – no full EIA or environmental registration is required for a software engineering office with no industrial installation, combustion plant, or polluting discharge.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No gaseous or wastewater process emissions arise; the office must still comply with general municipal wastewater rules, separate collection of electrical and electronic equipment waste under the WEEE regime, protected refrigerant handling in HVAC units, and the energy performance requirements for tertiary buildings under Luxembourg energy legislation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local commune fire authority, coordinated with the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS); occupancy permit and structural load clearance for office use; occupational health and safety registration with the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) once employees are engaged.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes, ACD) for direct taxes, and the Customs and Excise Agency (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA, AEDT) for VAT; primary digital portal: MyGuichet.lu (Guichet.lu) for all business tax e-filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing a Luxembourg presence must first register with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) through the single RCS e-filing to obtain the national business identification number (matricule). For a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), the GP or designated partner submits the incorporation deed and the standard registration forms on MyGuichet.lu. After RCS issuance, the entity obtains its VAT registration number from the AEDT by filing form 010/011 or via the e-space. A SCSp with no economic substance may not require a permanent establishment tax account, but shall obtain a standing tax file reference. Non-resident partners must each register for Luxembourg tax purposes if taxable income or a Luxembourg permanent establishment exists.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime. A SCSp is fiscally transparent by default for direct tax purposes; partners are taxed on their distributive share. There is no general statutory election to treat a SCSp as opaque for corporate income tax, but the Luxembourg tax administration accepts certain tailor-made tax opinions or rulings for transparency confirmation. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD (Law of 13 July 2021) apply and may reclassify payments to avoid double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée, TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual turnover (exclusive of VAT) for Luxembourg-established small taxpayers under the VAT lump-sum/small-business exemption; EUR 10,000 EU-wide threshold for cross-border distance sales of goods and certain B2C electronical supplies; non-established suppliers are generally subject to compulsory VAT registration on first taxable supply unless covered by the EU OSS scheme.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not currently mandate real-time e-invoicing clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping for B2B invoices. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only in the Business-to-Government (B2G) segment, using the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 format via the MyGuichet.lu platform. VAT returns are mandatory filed electronically using the structured eCDF file schema. No API-based fiscal stamping or pre-clearance is imposed as of 2025.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under Luxembourg VAT applies to goods dispatched or transported to a destination outside the EU by the supplier or on behalf of the customer, provided the goods leave the EU within statutory time limits. For offshore services such as software development and maintenance, export zero-rating or 'no place of supply in Luxembourg' treatment applies only if the B2B service is supplied to a business established in a third-country and is not physically performed in Luxembourg; the supplier must hold valid VAT number status evidence or other reasonable commercial information. The 0% rate is conditional on the exporter being able to demonstrate the physical movement out of the EU and the direct link between the supply and the exported goods.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (D.A.E. / SAD export declaration with approved exporter status or ExA)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note or other transport document evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg and arrival in a third country
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank statement or SWIFT confirmation proving settlement of the exported supply consideration within the payment term
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Luxembourg VAT administration conducts ex-post substance reviews on export zero-rating evidence, requiring the complete export file to be retained for at least 10 years. Fraudulent or unsubstantiated zero-rating claims trigger immediate recovery of the VAT not paid, penalty interest of 0.75% per month, fines up to the amount of tax evaded, and criminal penalties in cases of serious tax fraud under Article 58 of the General Tax Law. Repatriation deadlines are monitored; late foreign exchange receipts without valid commercial justification may lead to deemed export refund denial and clawback of input VAT credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) operating within the Eurosystem; prudential regulation and AML supervision by Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF); monetary policy and foreign exchange framework delegated to the European Central Bank (ECB) pursuant to TFEU Title IV and the ESCB Statute.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility on both current and capital account under EU free movement of capital (Articles 63–66 TFEU) and the Grand-Ducal Repeal of Exchange Control Regulations (1963 system abolished). No prior authorisation, licensing, or BCL approval is required for inward capital contributions, loan drawings, trade payments, dividends, or liquidation proceeds. Profit remittance friction is minimal: the SCSp is fiscally transparent, so distributions to non-resident partners are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, provided the partner is the effective beneficial owner and the income is not Luxembourg-source business profit attributable to a Luxembourg PE. CRS/FATCA reporting does apply; paying agents may request beneficial ownership and tax residency forms.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No export proceeds surrender requirement and no mandatory conversion ratio exist in Luxembourg legislation. Accounts receivable from offshore software development services may be retained freely in EUR or foreign currency, credited to any domestic or foreign account, and converted at any time without reporting approval. Only statistical balance-of-payments reporting obligations apply: Luxembourg resident credit institutions report individual cross-border transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 12,500 to the BCL under the ECB/BCL BOP framework; the SCSp itself has no direct filing duty.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational EUR Current Account with SEPA and SWIFT capabilities; segregated capital sub-ledger available
Operational Account plus Capital Escrow Account for partner commitments; treasury workstation access
Operational Account with Trade Finance and Commercial LC issuance facility
Operational Account with Cross-Border Cash Pooling and FX Forward lines
Transactional Account for Client Contract Proceeds and Supplier Payments
Private Banking Wealth Structure; not suitable for operational clearing

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-Medium. Wise Business and Payoneer are usable for small contract proceeds and sub-contractor payouts, but neither reliably supports MT103 inbound capital calls, SAP-style purpose-code formatting, or commercial LC instruments. Legally, a UK or EU-authorised EMI may onboard a Luxembourg SCSp under passporting, yet most EMIs lack the CDD framework to verify a partnership with non-resident partners and may reject the file as opaque-for-AML. Where accepted, monthly volume caps and limited routing options make the EMI channel supplementary only; the primary operating account should remain at a Tier 1 Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Hybrid mandate: CSSF anti-money-laundering law (12 Nov 2004 as amended) and CSSF video-identification circulars permit fully remote onboarding with a qualified electronic signature and certified video call when the UBO holds an EU-recognised e-ID and the risk score is low. In practice, BCEE, BIL, and Société Générale Luxembourg require at least one in-person meeting for partnership structures; the general partner's managing director (or a Luxembourg-regulated professional acting as introducer) must appear either physically at the bank's Luxembourg premises or through a CSSF-certified video identification session. A notarised or apostilled KYC dossier is commonly required for non-EU shareholders; if the GP is a Luxembourg S.à r.l., its own RCSL excerpt and UBO register extract must be submitted.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp opacity: the partnership may be unregistered at the RCSL and is not required to file publicly; bank cannot verify UBO chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised partnership agreement and any private side-letter; if RCSL-registered, a certified extract; Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) filing proof; full look-through diagram of general and limited partners; CVs of the general partner's directors; declaration of the partnership capital allocation percentages

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain crossing several jurisdictions creates complex ownership tracing
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBO declaration signed by the GP; passport copies and proof of address for all natural persons holding ≥25%; corporate registry excerpts and tax residency certificates for each intermediate entity; sanctions and PEP screening reports dated within 90 days; explanation of any nominee or trust layer

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore development centre substance risk: bank suspects a letterbox vehicle with no local activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid lease for the Luxembourg registered office; employment contracts and CCSS (Luxembourg social security) certificates for at least one resident director and two operational staff; client software development and maintenance agreements with fee schedules; monthly payroll evidence; issued invoices to overseas group entities; professional indemnity insurance certificate

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection from related offshore entities in low-tax jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Twelve months of bank statements of the contributing entity; source-of-wealth letter; the underlying commercial agreements generating the capital; tax residency certificate of the funding entity; clear statement that the contribution is booked as partnership capital and not shareholder loan; alignment of the injection with the RBE/CRS filings

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Outbound disbursements to high-risk developer jurisdictions (e.g., India, Vietnam, Ukraine, Serbia) for contractor payroll
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed sub-contracting or software development agreements; detailed invoice and deliverable schedule; ISO 20022 purpose code in each wire (e.g., SUPP for supplier payments); sanctions screening report on every beneficiary; internal AML risk assessment of the payment corridor; contractual right to conduct below-the-line audit on ultimate use of funds

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: EUR capital contributions routed via TARGET2/SEPA credit transfer for EU-origin funds (instant up to EUR 100,000, otherwise standard 1–2 business days); for non-EU sources, SWIFT MT103 with field 70 containing 'SCSP CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' and purpose code in line with the ISO 20022 semantics. The remitting bank is to be instructed that the account name and number must match the SCSp's own IBAN; a signed capital call letter addressed to the bank and held on file avoids delays. Foreign-currency injections are converted at a competitive FX rate on receipt; no BCL authorisation is required, but the bank will record the payment for BOP statistical reporting if above EUR 12,500.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Multi-rail clearing architecture: (1) SWIFT MT103 with explicit ISO purpose codes for international vendor, contractor, and licensing payments; (2) SEPA Credit Transfer for EU payroll and EU vendor settlements on 1-business-day execution with full IBAN validation; (3) Commercial Letter of Credit (SWIFT MT700) via Société Générale Luxembourg or BNP Paribas Luxembourg for hardware procurement and large software subcontracts payable 30–90 days after B/L or acceptance; (4) open-account settlement with dynamic discounting for investment-grade counterparties. All disbursements require dual approver control, an intraday liquidity forecast, and an FX execution memorandum captured at the time of order.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/INR, EUR/VND) up to 12 months under an ISDA 2002 or French FBF master agreement
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on INR, VND, PHP, and UAH for non-convertible or restricted currency corridors where local onshore deliverability fails
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD, EUR/INR) matched to multi-year client contracts for both interest and principal flows
European-style FX options on EUR/USD with premium paid upfront or zero-cost collars capped at a 30–40 delta band
Overnight/TOM/NEXT FX swaps for SEPA and correspondent account cash-sweep efficiency

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing with RCS (if SCSp exceeds small-undertaking thresholds)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after financial year-end; for a 31 December year-end, by 30 June of the following year. No extension is available.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €5,000 for late filing; repeated failure may lead to court-ordered strike-off (radiation) from the RCS and civil liability of the general partner for resulting damages.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner (UBO) register verification and update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Changes must be filed within 1 month of any change in beneficial ownership; a separate annual confirmation is not legally due, but an internal annual review must be completed by 31 March of the following year to certify the register as at 31 December.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines for non-disclosure or inaccurate UBO filings up to €1,250,000 for legal entities and up to €250,000 for natural persons; persistent violations can result in judicial strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual partnership tax information return (if taxable income is allocated to partners)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) – Luxembourg direct tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a December year-end, filing on or before 30 June of the following year (electronic filing); requests for extension may be granted by the local tax office.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties of 10% of net taxable amount (minimum €30); interest at 3% per month on outstanding assessments; failure may lead to official tax assessment and enforcement.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory audit becomes compulsory when the SCSp exceeds two of the following three thresholds in a given financial year: balance-sheet total > €4.4 million; net turnover > €8.8 million; average 50+ full-time employees. A mandatory audit is also required if the SCSp is a Credit-Category AIF or is otherwise supervised by the CSSF.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual financial statements must be prepared under Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 (as amended) and the 2016 Chart of Accounts. IFRS is permitted only where expressly opted or required for consolidated reporting by a listed parent.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Although Luxembourg does not require a separate annual UBO declaration form, the SCSp must implement an annual policy: (i) review the internal register of beneficial owners as at each 31 December; (ii) obtain and date a UBO self-declaration or certificate from each natural person owning or controlling >25% of partnership interests or voting rights; (iii) record any transfer of financial rights or voting interests in the partnership transfer register; and (iv) if a change occurred, file an updated UBO declaration with the RBE within one month of the triggering event. The annual confirmation does not relieve the SCSp of filing material changes during the year.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Partners (interest transfers and capital contributions)
Register of Appointments and Removals of General Partners and Managers
Minute Book containing partner resolutions and management approvals

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 550 – USD 2,200 per year depending on the corporate-services provider and service package
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 – USD 15,000 per engagement where an audit is mandatory; no audit fee arises for a small SCSp that remains below the statutory audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Luxembourg headline CIT is 17%, plus a 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax averaging 6.75%, producing an aggregate standard rate of approximately 24.94% for corporate partners. The SCSp itself is fiscally transparent and is not subject to Luxembourg CIT at entity level.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp entity-level rate: 0% because income is allocated to partners. Corporate partners with a Luxembourg taxable base may apply the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains, the Luxembourg IP Box (80% exemption of qualifying IP income giving an effective rate of approximately 5% on the qualifying margin), and OECD-compliant financing structures. The SCSp is not subject to minimum corporate income tax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Annual SCSp partnership transparency declaration (partnership annex in the Form 520 family), filed electronically through the Luxembourg Administration des contributions directes (ACD) e-filing portal accessible via MyGuichet.lu / MyTax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The SCSp itself files one transparency declaration; each corporate partner subject to Luxembourg CIT reports its allocable share through its own corporate return and pays quarterly advance CIT instalments.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For calendar-year entities, the ordinary annual filing deadline is 31 March following the tax year; the e-filing portal automatically extends this to 31 December. For non-calendar fiscal years, the return is due no later than the last day of the fifth month after the fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, RCS/Luxembourg business register number, Luxembourg tax number, registered office, date of incorporation, legal form and fiscal transparency status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Insert the Luxembourg tax number and RCS number of the SCSp. Non-resident partners are not listed as taxable entities on this box; they must be identified in the partner schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Balance sheet and profit and loss account of the SCSp, including accounting income before any partner-level adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The SCSp's accounting result is the starting point. No entity-level CIT is computed in this box; the result is simply allocated to partners according to the partnership agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Full details of every partner: name, residence, TIN, profit/loss sharing percentages, capital contributions, admission and exit dates, and changes in ownership during the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must provide their foreign TIN and treaty residence. Only Luxembourg-source income or income attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment is taxable in Luxembourg; foreign partners should assert treaty protection here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between the accounting result and the taxable allocation, including disallowed expenses, tax-exempt income, and any ATAD/GAAR adjustments relevant to Luxembourg partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should not automatically apply their domestic tax computations to this section; Luxembourg performs its own allocation only to the extent of Luxembourg nexus.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 - Transfer Pricing and Related-Party Transactions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all cross-border related-party transactions: software development fees, intercompany service charges, mark-ups, headcount, cost base, assumed risks, and the existence of contemporaneous TP documentation or a Luxembourg tax ruling.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the SCSp bills an offshore parent for ODC services, attach a benchmarking summary and explain why the cost-plus or TNMM result is arm's length. Non-resident partners cannot rely on the SCSp's tax transparency to avoid TP documentation obligations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts distributed or credited to partners during the year, including profit distributions, repayment of partner loans, interest, and royalties paid by the SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Profit distributions by a transparent SCSp are not dividends and are not subject to Luxembourg dividend withholding tax. Any contrary reclassification must be reported and documented, especially if Luxembourg real estate or a Luxembourg PE is involved.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts administrative fines up to EUR 25,000, daily discomfort/pressure fines if the taxpayer remains in default, and the loss of procedural deadlines. Late payment interest accrues at approximately 0.8% per month on partner-level liabilities. Deliberate false filing is criminal tax fraud, punishable by fines up to EUR 25,000 per count and imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax for dividends distributed by Luxembourg resident companies. A transparent SCSp's profit allocations are not dividends and are not subject to this 15% withholding.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: When withholding actually applies (e.g. dividends paid by a Luxembourg holding corporation through the SCSp structure), treaty relief is granted at source by submitting the Luxembourg ACD source-relief application, the valid tax residence certificate (TRC) of the beneficial owner, evidence of beneficial ownership, and, where relevant, the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive form for a qualified 10% corporate shareholder held for at least 12 months. If tax has been over-withheld, a refund is claimed through the ACD refund procedure using the TRC and supporting payment/reconciliation documents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Luxembourg withholding on outbound royalties and interest is generally 0% for corporate recipients. The former EU savings tax withholding no longer applies. Under Luxembourg's double tax treaties, interest and royalties are typically reduced to 0-10%, but because domestic law imposes no material B2B withholding, no treaty relief filing is required for ordinary cross-border interest or royalty payments.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 100,000 for annual related-party service transactions and EUR 1,000,000 for related-party goods transactions trigger mandatory Luxembourg Local File preparation. The Master File is required only where the worldwide group's consolidated revenue reaches EUR 750 million. Even below these thresholds, the ODC should maintain contemporaneous TP documentation because of the low-risk service-provider profile.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain sector-specific Economic Substance Regulations named as such, but economic substance is enforced through the Luxembourg GAAR, abuse-of-law jurisprudence, EU ATAD, and BEPS anti-abuse standards. The SCSp must demonstrate real local substance: physical office, Luxembourg-based decision-makers, locally contracted employees, local bank account, and actual performance of software engineering oversight. A pass-through invoicing vehicle with no local operational control will be recharacterized as a shell and denied tax treaty and EU directive benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Submitting false SCSp declarations, concealing partner income allocations, manufacturing invoices, using hidden e-wallet payment flows, or filing financial statements that contradict real cash movements.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all concealed profits with additional tax, administrative fraud penalties of up to 50% of the understated tax, fines up to EUR 25,000, and imprisonment up to five years for criminal tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto managers who participate in concealment are jointly and severally liable for unpaid tax and penalties. Courts may impose travel bans, asset freezing, civil restitution, disqualification from management, and imprisonment where bad faith is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The SCSp has no Luxembourg office, no Luxembourg employees, no local board decision-making, and functions solely as a billing intermediary for an offshore ODC while actual software delivery occurs elsewhere.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax authorities may disregard the SCSp as an abuse of law, reallocate income to the actual place of management, deny treaty and EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive benefits, and apply GAAR penalties up to 20% of the recharacterized benefit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing false substance declarations exposes directors to civil liability to investors and creditors, veil-piercing claims, forfeiture of management rights, and criminal forgery sanctions. Under evolving EU anti-shell rules, the resident director can become personally liable for the difference between substance and turnover.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Mispricing and Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging zero or below-cost markup on ODC services, bearing no economic risk while taking no reward, paying artificial royalties to a shell IP-owner, or failing to produce a Local File after exceeding the EUR 100,000 service threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary transfer pricing adjustment increasing Luxembourg taxable income to the arm's-length amount, late interest at 0.8% per month, penalties up to 20% of the adjustment in serious cases, and separate fines for incomplete Master/Local File documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who deliberately set non-arm's-length prices to strip Luxembourg profits are personally exposed to restitution of the extra taxes assessed on the partners and to disqualification orders. The tax administration may treat the arrangement as criminal fraud where the pricing structure is merely a sham.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering and Beneficial Ownership Violations
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using unregulated Wise/Payoneer accounts to receive client money, processing payments without a commercial substance check, concealing the ultimate beneficial owner from the RBS/beneficial ownership register, or accepting funds inconsistent with the ODC service contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF AML fines can reach EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover for severe violations; criminal money laundering is punishable by imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 1.25 million, increased for continuous or habitual laundering.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managers knowingly operating payment structures designed to obscure beneficial ownership face personal criminal liability, asset freezes, travel bans, extradition proceedings, and imprisonment. The corporate veil is lifted because the SCSp is a façade for illegal financial flows.
